final_recommendation: The room converged on filing the litigation notice within two weeks regardless of settlement signals, weaponizing market repricing data as evidence and regulatory pressure. A one-week ultimatum for concrete recovery terms was issued to force FINMA's hand, with the creditor group accepting that 150-200 bps repricing is inevitable and choosing to own the litigation momentum rather than wait.
minority_objections: FINMA legal argued a pre-filing settlement signal (partial recovery framework via resolution fund) could stop litigation acceleration and cap repricing damage at current levels, but this was rejected as theater without concrete numbers
key_conflicts: Whether settlement talks before filing could prevent 150-200 bps repricing spike (FINMA legal) vs. creditor view that repricing hits either way and filing owns momentum
Timing tension: FINMA needs days to table credible settlement vs. creditor two-week notice deadline already set
Whether precedent damage is already fully priced vs. litigation risk as accelerant requiring separate response
key_concessions: Credit analyst acknowledged repricing damage has both precedent (already baked) and litigation risk (accelerant) components, not either/or
FINMA legal implicitly conceded settlement must come within days (not weeks) to be credible
Bondholder group accepted that repricing will hit regardless, shifting focus to owning litigation momentum rather than preventing damage
red_lines: Creditors will not delay notice filing for settlement talks without concrete recovery numbers on the table
Any settlement framework must admit AT1 had salvageable value (which FINMA cannot do without proving write-down was discretionary)
Discovery of internal FINMA/UBS documents on viability finding and AT1 recovery value is non-negotiable once notice filed
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Systemic stability impact of 150-200 bps repricing on all European bank AT1 refinancing was acknowledged but not treated as a constraint on litigation strategy
Reputational damage to Switzerland's financial center from protracted litigation received no discussion
Possibility that discovery could reveal facts unfavorable to creditors (e.g., genuine viability concerns) was not explored
Coordination risk among diverse creditor group (retail vs institutional, different jurisdictions) not addressed despite joint action requirements
downstream_risk_variables: 150-200 bps AT1 repricing spike triggers refinancing pressure across European banking sector within 30 days of notice
Discovery process pulls FINMA internal emails, UBS valuation models, and legal opinions on AT1 recovery value
E&O and D&O claims against advisers who flagged AT1 recovery risk but proceeded with write-down
Multi-year claims tail across jurisdictions as creditor group pursues parallel litigation strategies
Regulatory legitimacy erosion if emergency ordinance necessity finding cannot withstand judicial scrutiny
Contagion to other resolution regimes as AT1 investors reprice sovereign discretion risk globally
uncertainty_notes: Whether FINMA can credibly table concrete recovery numbers within days (before notice filing) remains unresolved. The room did not establish whether the emergency ordinance's necessity finding can survive discovery showing AT1 had recovery value, nor whether a partial settlement could actually stop the repricing cascade once litigation momentum builds. The composition and coordination capacity of the creditor group was assumed but not validated.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Notice filing in two weeks was the room's central decision point, with all other strategies (settlement talks, ultimatum, joint statement) structured around litigation momentum as primary leverage
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Discovery of FINMA's viability event finding and whether AT1 had salvageable value drove the entire litigation strategy; proving write-down was discretionary (not emergency) was the core legal theory
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion was the foundational argument ('defensible only if emergency powers override creditor law') but was means to litigation end rather than independently driving the room's direction
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: 150-200 bps repricing within 30 days was treated as inevitable consequence and weaponized as evidence/pressure; market stabilization planning explicitly structured around this damage
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year E&O/D&O exposure from discovery was identified and quantified as substantial, but remained secondary to immediate litigation filing decision rather than shaping strategy
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O and E&O tail for advisers was explicitly surfaced with discovery mechanics (memos, valuations, legal opinions), but insurance observer's questions were not developed into structured risk assessment
